bull.t: Low leverage and stronger equity base
bull.b: Very low debt and the shift to strongly positive equity provide financial flexibility for an early-stage biotech. The roughly $172.1M TTM equity and $179.4M asset base can support ongoing development while limiting leverage-related pressure.

Precision oncology aimed at genetically defined cancers gives OnKure a focused development model rather than a broad, undifferentiated approach. If targeted programs advance, this specialization can support clearer patient selection and differentiated therapeutic positioning.

bull.t: Retention plan without stated added dilution
bull.b: Repricing existing underwater options may help retain employees and consultants during development, with 12–18 month service requirements. Because share counts and vesting were unchanged and no new grants or cash compensation were added, the measure seeks incentive alignment without additional stated dilution.

bear.t: No commercial revenue and widening losses
bear.b: Zero revenue across 2021–2025 and TTM, combined with persistent operating losses, shows the company has not yet established a commercial revenue base. Net loss widened to about $59.5M in 2025 and remained about $58.7M in TTM, leaving profitability dependent on future development success.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn and funding dependence
bear.b: Consistently negative operating and free cash flow, including roughly -$51.8M FCF in 2025 and -$47.9M TTM, indicates substantial ongoing cash consumption. Without internally generated cash, continued funding needs can constrain strategic flexibility and create dilution risk.

bear.t: Capital base is not generating returns
bear.b: Deeply negative returns on equity in profitable-equity periods, including roughly -0.49 in TTM, show that the enlarged capital base is not yet producing returns. This indicates that ongoing losses are consuming economic value despite the balance sheet’s improved equity position.
